practiceNotes: This is a curriculum proposal, not certification, authorization or an applied program.
Use spaced retrieval for concepts, representations, assumptions, counterexamples and method selection. Assess proof writing, programming, laboratory technique and extended inference separately.

Programming assessments should include unseen tests, reproducible environments, code review and explanations of failures; supplied software does not replace assessments of explicitly required implementations.
Wet laboratories require appropriate facilities, training, supervision, waste handling and institution-specific risk approval. Use nonpathogenic organisms and nonhazardous substitutes where possible.

Human-participant, animal and identifiable genomic-data work requires the applicable consent, ethics review, welfare provisions and data governance. Public or synthetic datasets can support many assessments.
Radiation, lasers, high voltage, pressure systems and reactive chemicals require professionally approved controls; use archived data or safe apparatus where authorization is absent.
Security experiments must run only on owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems. Robotics practice should begin in simulation and use physical emergency stops when hardware is introduced.
Fieldwork requires access permissions, ecological impact controls and accessible alternatives. Clinical examples are for scientific reasoning, not patient-specific treatment.
Graduate projects should include replication, uncertainty analysis, negative results and a critique of model assumptions, not only a successful demonstration.

outcomes.description: Decode packet encapsulation, addressing and name resolution across network layers.
Calculate routing, retransmission and congestion behavior in small network models.
Build socket clients and servers and diagnose failures from packet traces.

practice: Implement a reliable message protocol over simulated loss and analyze packet captures.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Organize, query and preserve structured information.
decks.title: Databases and Retrieval Foundations

outcomes.description: Design normalized schemas and express correct relational-algebra and SQL queries.
Implement index and join methods and compare query execution costs.
Analyze serializability and construct locking, logging and recovery schedules.
Build an inverted index and evaluate TF-IDF ranking using precision and recall.

practice: Build a small storage/query engine and a lexical document search system with relevance judgments.

includes: Binding, closures, effects and evaluation order

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Explain language behavior through formal models.
decks.title: Programming Languages

outcomes.description: Define small-step semantics and implement a matching interpreter.
Construct typing derivations and prove progress and preservation for a small language.
Compare binding, evaluation and effect mechanisms using distinguishing programs.

practice: Implement typed interpreters and prove a restricted language-safety theorem.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Translate source programs into correct executable code.
decks.title: Compiler Construction

outcomes.description: Construct lexical and grammar-based parsers with informative error recovery.
Implement intermediate representations and semantics-preserving dataflow optimizations.
Generate machine code with instruction selection, register allocation and calling conventions.

practice: Build an end-to-end compiler and differential-test it against an interpreter.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Characterize what formal machines can compute.
decks.title: Theory of Computation

outcomes.description: Construct automata and grammars and prove language closure and nonmembership results.
Construct machine reductions and prove decidability, recognizability and undecidability claims.

practice: Design machines and write reductions with explicit input transformations and equivalences.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Analyze computational feasibility and its theoretical limits.
decks.title: Computational Complexity

outcomes.description: Prove completeness results and compare time and space classes using reductions.
Analyze randomized algorithms, amplification and basic interactive-proof protocols.
Prove approximation guarantees and establish representative approximation hardness reductions.

practice: Write completeness proofs and analyze randomized and approximation algorithms.

includes: Bayesian networks and finite decision processes

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Build agents that search, reason and act under uncertainty.
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence

outcomes.description: Implement heuristic search and constraint propagation and justify completeness conditions.
Represent knowledge and construct sound inference and symbolic planning procedures.
Perform finite Bayesian-network inference and value iteration for decision processes.

practice: Implement a planning agent and compare heuristic and probabilistic decisions on controlled tasks.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Construct and critically evaluate predictive models.
decks.title: Machine Learning

outcomes.description: Implement regularized linear, logistic and tree-based predictors with appropriate losses.
Implement k-means, mixture-model EM and principal-component analysis and diagnose failures.
Design leakage-resistant evaluation and assess calibration, subgroup harms and deployment shift.

practice: Build reproducible prediction pipelines with held-out evaluation and an evidence-based deployment recommendation.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Develop graduate learning theory and modern learning methods.
decks.title: Advanced Statistical Learning

outcomes.description: Derive representative capacity and stability generalization bounds and explain their limits.
Implement automatic differentiation and train convolutional and attention models with ablations.
Derive and implement temporal-difference and policy-gradient methods and assess off-policy risks.

practice: Replicate a learning result with a small implementation, theoretical analysis and failure-focused ablations.

includes: User research and cognitive task models

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Design and evaluate systems around human capabilities and needs.
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction

outcomes.description: Conduct interviews and task analysis and translate findings into design requirements.
Build interactive prototypes using event-driven interface programming taught locally.
Design usability studies and accessibility audits and justify privacy and inclusion decisions.

practice: Iterate a prototype using consented usability evidence and keyboard/screen-reader accessibility tests.

includes: Reflectance, ray tracing and Monte Carlo rendering

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Construct images from geometric and light-transport models.
decks.title: Computer Graphics

outcomes.description: Implement camera transforms, mesh representations and geometric intersections.
Implement clipping, rasterization, depth testing and antialiasing.
Derive a bounded rendering equation and implement Monte Carlo path tracing with variance checks.

practice: Build software rasterizers and path tracers and compare image error against sample count.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Engineer defenses against explicit adversarial capabilities.
decks.title: Security Engineering

outcomes.description: Construct threat models and justify controls, disclosure decisions and residual risks.
Diagnose and repair memory, injection, authentication and privilege-boundary vulnerabilities.
Select and correctly use authenticated encryption, signatures and secure-channel protocols.

practice: Audit and harden a deliberately vulnerable isolated service, documenting authorization and residual risk.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Prove security claims under explicit computational assumptions.
decks.title: Cryptographic Foundations

outcomes.description: Formalize adversarial games and construct reductions with quantified advantage bounds.
Prove representative encryption and authentication constructions from pseudorandom primitives.
Analyze number-theoretic key exchange, encryption and signatures under stated assumptions.

practice: Write game-based security proofs and construct counterattacks to weakened definitions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Coordinate computation despite concurrency and partial failure.
decks.title: Distributed and Parallel Computing

outcomes.description: Analyze logical clocks, replication and consistency models using execution histories.
Implement consensus and recovery protocols and explain impossibility under stated failure models.
Implement shared-memory and message-passing decomposition and measure communication and scaling limits.

practice: Build a replicated service with fault injection and parallelize a workload using taught thread and message APIs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Verify executable systems against formal specifications.
decks.title: Formal Verification

outcomes.description: Specify and prove partial and total correctness using invariants and termination measures.
Implement finite-state temporal model checking and interpret abstraction counterexamples.
Mechanize small program proofs using locally taught proof-assistant tactics and trusted-kernel concepts.

practice: Verify a data structure and model-check a protocol, reporting specification and abstraction limitations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.description: Integrate perception, planning and control for embodied systems.
decks.title: Robotics and Geometric Vision

outcomes.description: Calibrate cameras and estimate geometric correspondences and three-dimensional structure.
Derive rigid-body forward and inverse kinematics and manipulator Jacobians.
Implement configuration-space search and sampling-based collision-free motion planning.
Integrate state estimation and feedback and evaluate safety under sensing and actuator errors.

practice: Implement a simulated visual-navigation or manipulation system and run controlled failure and safety tests.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: An accessible entry to physical modeling and evidence.
decks.title: Physical Foundations

outcomes.description: Use dimensional analysis and estimate measurement resolution and repeatability.
Solve constant-acceleration and static-force problems using vectors and diagrams.
Calculate work, energy and power in simple systems and identify model boundaries.

practice: Measure motion with simple apparatus and compare algebraic models against uncertainty-aware data.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Apply Newtonian laws to quantitative mechanical systems.
decks.title: Newtonian Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive and solve particle equations with position- or velocity-dependent forces.
Apply momentum, angular momentum and energy balances to collisions and constrained motion.
Calculate rigid-body inertia and central-force orbital quantities.

practice: Derive mechanics models from free-body diagrams and test conservation against measured trajectories.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Connect local oscillation to propagating disturbances.
decks.title: Oscillations and Waves

outcomes.description: Derive oscillator response, resonance and energy dissipation.
Calculate normal modes of coupled systems and interpret mode excitation.
Derive the one-dimensional wave equation and calculate reflection, interference and acoustic intensity.

practice: Analyze coupled oscillators and measure resonance and standing-wave patterns.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: An operational entry to electrical and magnetic models.
decks.title: Electricity and Magnetism

outcomes.description: Calculate electric fields, potentials and capacitance for simple charge geometries.
Solve resistor networks and derive elementary RC transients by separation.
Calculate magnetic forces, flux changes and induced electromotive forces in simple geometries.

practice: Construct low-voltage circuits and compare potential, current and transient measurements with models.

includes: Thermal state variables and energy balance

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Reason macroscopically about heat, work and equilibrium.
decks.title: Thermal Physics

outcomes.description: Apply equations of state and the first law to quasistatic and heat-transfer processes.
Calculate entropy changes and engine bounds and distinguish reversible from irreversible paths.
Use total differentials and thermodynamic potentials to determine equilibrium and stability.

practice: Analyze cycles, calorimetry and phase changes with complete energy and entropy accounts.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Accessible conceptual and algebraic entry to modern physics.
decks.title: Modern Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz transformations, intervals and relativistic energy-momentum balances.
Analyze photon, diffraction and discrete-spectrum evidence using explicitly stated quantum models.
Estimate atomic energies, nuclear binding and exponential radioactive decay.

practice: Reconstruct historical experimental arguments and solve algebraic relativistic and quantum-scale problems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Reformulate mechanics through action and phase space.
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations and apply generalized coordinates to constrained systems.
Construct Hamiltonians and derive phase-space evolution and Poisson-bracket relations.
Use canonical transformations and Noether's theorem to identify conserved quantities.

practice: Derive constrained and central-force systems in both Lagrangian and Hamiltonian forms.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Solve classical field problems at graduate depth.
decks.title: Classical Electrodynamics

outcomes.description: Derive and solve Maxwell boundary problems using multipoles and Green functions.
Calculate retarded potentials, dipole radiation and field energy-momentum flux.
Construct four-vectors and field tensors and transform electromagnetic equations covariantly.

practice: Solve boundary-value and radiation problems and verify limiting cases and conservation laws.

includes: Complex state spaces and Schrodinger dynamics

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Calculate quantum predictions and their operational interpretation.
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Use complex amplitudes, operators and measurement rules to solve standard quantum dynamics.
Derive angular-momentum spectra and combine orbital and spin states.
Apply perturbation, variational, WKB and elementary scattering approximations with validity checks.
Construct symmetrized states and reduced density matrices and interpret exchange and entanglement.

practice: Derive bound-state, spin and scattering predictions and compare approximation errors.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Derive macroscopic behavior from microscopic statistics.
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive ensemble distributions and thermodynamic observables from partition functions.
Calculate Bose and Fermi gas properties and explain classical limits.
Analyze ordering, correlations and critical scaling using mean-field and coarse-graining models.

practice: Derive equations of state and compare exact, mean-field and scaling predictions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Produce defensible physical measurements.
decks.title: Experimental Physics Methods

outcomes.description: Calibrate sensors and characterize amplification, bandwidth, loading and noise.
Construct uncertainty budgets with covariance and evaluate fit residuals and systematic errors.
Design discriminating experiments and justify controls, safety decisions and reproducible records.

practice: Build and calibrate a low-voltage sensor chain and compare competing physical models using raw data.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Predict image formation and optical measurement limits.
decks.title: Optics

outcomes.description: Design paraxial imaging systems and calculate aberration and resolution tradeoffs.
Calculate interference and diffraction patterns with coherence and aperture effects.
Use polarization matrices and Fourier transfer methods to analyze optical systems.

practice: Design an imaging or interferometric experiment and recover aperture information from diffraction data.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Model flowing continua with explicit constitutive assumptions.
decks.title: Fluid Mechanics

outcomes.description: Derive continuity and Navier-Stokes equations from control-volume balances.
Solve representative potential, pipe, creeping and boundary-layer flows.
Use nondimensionalization and linear perturbations to assess similarity and flow instability.

practice: Derive flow solutions and compare dimensionless predictions with pipe or public wind-tunnel data.

includes: Linear elasticity and structural boundary problems

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Analyze deformation and mechanical failure of solids.
decks.title: Solid Continuum Mechanics

outcomes.description: Construct stress and strain tensors and transform principal components.
Derive elastic balance equations and solve beam and elementary continuum boundary problems.
Apply yield criteria and energy-based fracture models with explicit applicability limits.

practice: Analyze load-deformation and crack-growth datasets and compare constitutive assumptions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Explain emergent properties of many-particle materials.
decks.title: Condensed Matter Physics

outcomes.description: Construct reciprocal lattices and derive nearly-free and tight-binding electronic bands.
Calculate phonon spectra and elementary electronic and thermal transport coefficients.
Analyze magnetic and superconducting models and calculate a simple band-topology invariant.

practice: Derive model band structures and interpret diffraction, heat-capacity and transport evidence.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Connect nuclear models to measured reactions and radiation.
decks.title: Nuclear Physics

outcomes.description: Estimate nuclear binding and explain shell, spin and collective structure evidence.
Calculate decay chains, reaction thresholds and elementary cross sections.
Interpret detector spectra, counting uncertainty, attenuation and absorbed-dose estimates.

practice: Analyze archived gamma spectra and reaction data with efficiency and background corrections.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Interpret particle models and collision experiments.
decks.title: Particle Physics

outcomes.description: Classify particles and apply conservation and symmetry rules to allowed interactions.
Calculate invariant masses, thresholds and two-body decay kinematics using four-vectors.
Infer particle signals from event distributions while accounting for backgrounds and detector acceptance.

practice: Reconstruct resonances from public collision events and critique discovery claims.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Infer cosmic properties from limited observations.
decks.title: Astrophysics and Cosmology

outcomes.description: Infer luminosities, distances and composition from photometry and spectral models taught locally.
Derive hydrostatic stellar estimates and explain energy generation and evolutionary endpoints.
Analyze rotation curves and fit bounded expansion models while distinguishing observational degeneracies.

practice: Analyze public stellar and galaxy catalogs and propagate selection and distance uncertainties.

includes: Black holes, waves and homogeneous cosmology

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Model gravity as dynamical spacetime geometry.
decks.title: General Relativity

outcomes.description: Calculate proper time, geodesics and tidal effects in Lorentzian metrics.
Derive Einstein equations from an action and recover the Newtonian limit.
Analyze Schwarzschild, weak-wave and Friedmann solutions and their observational implications.

practice: Derive spacetime observables and solve black-hole and cosmological limiting cases.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Develop established quantum-field working methods.
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory

outcomes.description: Quantize free scalar, spinor and electromagnetic fields and construct particle states.
Derive propagators and Feynman rules and calculate elementary scattering amplitudes.
Regularize representative loop integrals and explain renormalized parameters and gauge constraints.

practice: Derive tree-level amplitudes and a simple one-loop correction with explicit conventions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Compare particle, fluid and kinetic plasma descriptions.
decks.title: Plasma Physics

outcomes.description: Calculate gyro-motion, drifts and adiabatic invariants in prescribed fields.
Derive plasma-fluid and MHD wave relations and assess basic instabilities.
Derive kinetic response from Vlasov models and calculate collisionless damping.

practice: Derive dispersion relations and compare kinetic and fluid predictions across scale regimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.description: Investigate nonlinear physical behavior reproducibly.
decks.title: Nonlinear and Computational Physics

outcomes.description: Derive local bifurcation normal forms and continue equilibria numerically.
Construct Poincare maps and estimate Lyapunov exponents while distinguishing numerical artifacts.
Implement symplectic and finite-difference physical models and verify conservation and grid convergence.

practice: Investigate a nonlinear oscillator and derive a locally taught finite-difference diffusion model with convergence tests.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Build the representational language of chemistry.
decks.title: Chemical Foundations

outcomes.description: Balance reactions and calculate composition, limiting reagents and yields.
Use electron configurations, Lewis structures and geometry to predict bonding and polarity.
Relate intermolecular forces and enthalpy changes to physical and chemical transformations.

practice: Translate particle, structural and symbolic representations and solve quantitative reaction problems.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Calculate chemical composition in reacting solutions.
decks.title: Chemical Equilibrium

outcomes.description: Set up mass-action, material and charge balances and justify equilibrium approximations.
Calculate pH, buffer capacity and titration behavior for common acid-base systems.
Predict precipitation and metal speciation using coupled solubility and complexation equilibria.

practice: Solve coupled equilibrium cases and audit approximation errors by back-substitution.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Perform and document foundational chemical operations.
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Foundations

outcomes.description: Prepare standardized solutions and perform titrations with traceable concentration calculations.
Perform elementary separations and calculate recovery, replicate precision and propagated resolution limits.
Create auditable records and justify chemical handling, incompatibility and waste-control decisions.

practice: Prepare and assay an unknown solution and separate a safe mixture with a written risk assessment.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Reason about three-dimensional organic molecules.
decks.title: Organic Structure and Stereochemistry

outcomes.description: Translate organic names and line structures and assign resonance and functional groups.
Assign stereochemical relationships and configurations and predict stereoisomer counts.
Analyze conformer populations and structural effects on acidity and intermolecular properties.

practice: Use drawings and molecular models to solve stereochemical and conformational problems.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Predict organic reactivity from mechanistic evidence.
decks.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms

outcomes.description: Predict substitution, elimination and alkene-addition outcomes with kinetic and stereochemical reasoning.
Construct carbonyl and enolate mechanisms and predict chemoselective products.
Explain aromatic substitution and common oxidation-reduction transformations through electron flow.

practice: Solve unfamiliar mechanism and product-prediction problems with competing-pathway explanations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Design and evaluate multistep molecular construction.
decks.title: Organic Synthesis

outcomes.description: Construct feasible retrosynthetic routes using disconnections and functional-group interconversions.
Choose protecting groups and stereochemical strategies and compare step-economy tradeoffs.
Plan reaction workup and purification and validate identity, yield and purity.

practice: Compare multistep routes and execute an approved short synthesis or audit a complete experimental record.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Explain inorganic structure and reactivity across the periodic table.
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry

outcomes.description: Predict main-group structures and reactions using periodic and oxidation-state trends.
Analyze coordination geometry, isomerism, ligand substitution and elementary crystal-field splitting.
Relate packing, lattice energy and bonding to inorganic-solid properties.

practice: Interpret inorganic reaction and magnetic-property evidence and construct coordination isomers.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Apply thermodynamic theory to chemical composition and phases.
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics

outcomes.description: Derive chemical-potential and equilibrium-constant relations from free-energy changes.
Construct and interpret phase diagrams and derive coexistence slopes and phase rules.
Calculate activities and partial molar properties and diagnose ideal-solution failures.

practice: Infer phase and equilibrium parameters from thermochemical and vapor-pressure datasets.

includes: Homogeneous, enzyme and surface catalysis kinetics

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Infer and test time-dependent chemical mechanisms.
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics

outcomes.description: Estimate integrated rate laws and Arrhenius parameters with residual and uncertainty checks.
Derive network rate equations and assess steady-state and pre-equilibrium approximations.
Derive saturation and surface-catalysis rate laws and distinguish kinetic inhibition mechanisms.

practice: Analyze time-course data and discriminate mechanisms using independently varied concentrations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Apply quantum mechanics to molecular structure and observables.
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive molecular-orbital models and variational electronic-energy approximations.
Construct point-group representations and symmetry-adapted orbital combinations using character tables.
Calculate molecular energy levels, transition intensities and symmetry selection rules.

practice: Derive small-molecule orbital and spectral predictions and compare them with measured spectra.

includes: Atomic, optical and mass analytical instruments

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Develop defensible chemical measurement methods.
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry

outcomes.description: Validate assays using blanks, standards, recovery, detection limits and uncertainty budgets.
Calculate retention, efficiency and resolution and optimize chromatographic separations.
Explain instrument signal generation and select methods against matrix, selectivity and sensitivity constraints.

practice: Develop and validate an assay from sampling plan through calibration and independent quality controls.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Determine molecular structure from complementary spectra.
decks.title: Structure Elucidation and Spectroscopy

outcomes.description: Interpret IR and electronic spectra using locally defined energy-level and oscillator models.
Assign elementary one- and two-dimensional NMR spectra using shifts, integrals and coupling.
Interpret isotope and fragmentation patterns and integrate spectra into defensible structural assignments.

practice: Solve blinded structure-elucidation cases and state which alternative structures remain possible.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Connect chemical reactions to electrical transport and devices.
decks.title: Electrochemistry

outcomes.description: Derive Nernst relations and calculate electrochemical equilibrium and cell work.
Apply Butler-Volmer and diffusion-layer models to current-overpotential behavior.
Interpret voltammograms and diagnose battery limitations and corrosion-control strategies.

practice: Analyze electrochemical datasets using explicit charge-transfer and one-dimensional transport models taught locally.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Relate preparation and chemical structure to material function.
decks.title: Materials Chemistry

outcomes.description: Design solid-state or solution synthesis and calculate defect and stoichiometry balances.
Index simple diffraction patterns using locally derived Bragg geometry and interpret thermal analyses.
Analyze adsorption, surface energy and interfacial reactions in catalysts and nanomaterials.

practice: Plan a material synthesis and infer phase purity, defects and surface behavior from characterization data.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Connect macromolecular synthesis to chain-scale behavior.
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive step- and chain-growth relations and choose polymerization control strategies.
Calculate molecular-weight averages and ideal-chain size distributions.
Interpret glass transitions, viscoelastic response and processing-property tradeoffs using bounded constitutive models.

practice: Predict molecular-weight distributions and interpret thermal and rheological polymer datasets.

includes: Protein, nucleic-acid, lipid and carbohydrate chemistry

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Explain the chemical organization of living systems.
decks.title: Biochemistry

outcomes.description: Relate biomolecular structures and noncovalent interactions to folding, binding and membrane assembly.
Interpret enzyme saturation, inhibition and allostery using algebraic binding and rate models.
Trace metabolic carbon, electrons and ATP coupling and predict regulation under altered conditions.

practice: Analyze enzyme and metabolic perturbation datasets and explain molecular mechanisms without relying on pathway-name recall.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Predict metal-centered electronic structure and catalysis.
decks.title: Advanced Inorganic and Organometallic Chemistry

outcomes.description: Derive ligand-field orbital schemes and interpret magnetic and electronic spectra.
Predict organometallic elementary steps using electron counts, orbital interactions and stereochemistry.
Construct catalytic cycles and discriminate resting states and rate-controlling pathways.

practice: Propose and test catalytic-cycle hypotheses against kinetic, isotopic and spectroscopic evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Produce reproducible molecular calculations with controlled approximations.
decks.title: Computational Chemistry

outcomes.description: Implement a small self-consistent-field calculation and compare established electronic-structure approximations.
Implement force-field dynamics and Metropolis sampling and estimate equilibrium observables.
Assess basis, convergence, sampling and model errors against independent reference evidence.

practice: Build small SCF and molecular-simulation implementations and audit a published computational claim.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Connect microscopic motion to measured chemical rates.
decks.title: Reaction Dynamics

outcomes.description: Derive transition-state and unimolecular rate expressions and assess tunneling and recrossing corrections.
Analyze reactive pathways and elementary nonadiabatic transitions on coupled potential surfaces.
Infer dynamical mechanisms from time-resolved signals with instrument-response and identifiability checks.

practice: Derive rate predictions and analyze supplied pump-probe traces using locally taught convolution models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Use mechanistic theory to design demanding organic transformations.
decks.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry

outcomes.description: Predict pericyclic and photochemical selectivity using orbital-symmetry arguments.
Design asymmetric transformations and rationalize stereocontrol with competing transition-state models.
Discriminate mechanisms using isotope effects, substituent correlations and kinetic evidence.

practice: Defend a stereoselective route and design experiments that separate rival mechanistic explanations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.description: Track chemicals through environmental compartments.
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry

outcomes.description: Calculate equilibrium partitioning and compartment mass balances for environmental contaminants.
Construct bounded atmospheric and aquatic reaction networks and estimate transformation lifetimes.
Design monitoring and compare remediation options using exposure, uncertainty and distributive-impact evidence.

practice: Construct a contaminant fate assessment with sampled-data uncertainty and a justified remediation recommendation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Accessible entry to living systems and biological evidence.
decks.title: Biological Foundations

outcomes.description: Compare cellular organization, energy acquisition and homeostasis across living systems.
Explain inheritance, variation and selection without confusing individual change with population evolution.
Interpret simple biological tables and diagrams and distinguish observation from causal evidence.

practice: Build evidence-based explanations from organism observations and simple proportional data taught locally.

includes: Microbial, fungal, plant and animal diversity

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Recognize biological diversity through shared ancestry and form.
decks.title: Organismal Diversity

outcomes.description: Identify major lineages from diagnostic cellular, anatomical and life-cycle traits.
Compare body plans and reproductive strategies and distinguish homology from convergence.
Read phylogenetic trees and map character changes without ladder-like evolutionary interpretations.

practice: Construct comparative character matrices from specimens, images and life-cycle observations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain cellular organization and regulated function.
decks.title: Cell Biology

outcomes.description: Relate compartment, cytoskeletal and trafficking organization to cellular functions.
Predict diffusion, osmosis and carrier-mediated transport using explicit gradient and saturation models.
Explain cell-cycle checkpoints and signaling logic and predict consequences of disrupted control.

practice: Interpret localization, transport and checkpoint perturbation experiments.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer inheritance mechanisms from crosses and pedigrees.
decks.title: Genetics

outcomes.description: Predict crosses and pedigrees and estimate recombination maps from segregation data.
Explain mutation, chromosome rearrangement and dosage effects using genotype-to-phenotype evidence.
Interpret additive inheritance, heritability and gene-environment interaction without deterministic overclaims.

practice: Solve linkage and pedigree cases and critique causal claims based on heritability estimates.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain information processing through molecular mechanisms.
decks.title: Molecular Biology

outcomes.description: Explain replication, recombination and repair mechanisms and predict genome-instability phenotypes.
Trace transcription, RNA processing and translation and interpret perturbation evidence.
Infer transcriptional, chromatin and post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms from controlled experiments.

practice: Analyze gene-expression and DNA-repair experiments and propose discriminating molecular tests.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Generate and evaluate reproducible biological measurements.
decks.title: Experimental Biology Methods

outcomes.description: Calibrate microscopy images and quantify cells using explicit segmentation and sampling rules.
Explain and perform extraction, electrophoresis and PCR with contamination and specificity controls.
Design replicated biological studies and justify controls, blinding, welfare and data-integrity decisions.

practice: Complete a safe microscopy and molecular-assay study with raw images, controls and preregistered analysis rules.

includes: Circulation, respiration, digestion and renal regulation

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain animal function through coupled organ systems.
decks.title: Animal Anatomy and Physiology

outcomes.description: Explain action potentials, synapses and muscle contraction using locally defined electrochemical models.
Analyze organ exchange and homeostasis using algebraic flow, diffusion and mass-balance models.
Predict endocrine and reproductive responses to perturbations in feedback pathways.

practice: Interpret physiological time series and compare compensatory responses across organ systems and species.

includes: Plant growth, reproduction and environmental responses

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain plant function in its structural and environmental context.
decks.title: Plant Biology

outcomes.description: Relate root, shoot and vascular anatomy to water and assimilate transport.
Explain photosynthetic pathways and nutrient acquisition and predict resource-limitation responses.
Analyze hormone, light and stress regulation of plant development and reproduction.

practice: Investigate safe plant growth and water-status perturbations with explicit physiological predictions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain microbial and viral strategies across environments.
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology

outcomes.description: Measure microbial growth by dilution and counts and interpret culture and viability biases.
Compare microbial metabolic strategies, symbioses and biogeochemical roles.
Explain viral replication, host range and horizontal genetic transfer and infer lifecycle stages.

practice: Analyze safe culture or archived growth data and reconstruct viral lifecycles from experimental observations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain protective and pathological immune responses.
decks.title: Immunology

outcomes.description: Trace innate sensing, inflammatory signaling and antigen presentation during infection.
Explain receptor diversification, lymphocyte selection and adaptive immune memory.
Discriminate mechanisms of allergy, autoimmunity and immunodeficiency using experimental evidence.

practice: Interpret immune-cell, antibody and perturbation datasets and compare protective versus damaging responses.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain how regulated cell behavior builds organisms.
decks.title: Developmental Biology

outcomes.description: Infer cell-fate and positional-information mechanisms from lineage and signaling evidence.
Explain tissue shape changes through adhesion, polarity and coordinated cell movements.
Interpret developmental perturbations and compare conserved mechanisms across organismal body plans.

practice: Construct causal developmental models from fate maps, mutant phenotypes and live-image sequences.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Connect cellular signals to circuits and behavior.
decks.title: Neuroscience

outcomes.description: Quantify spike rates, tuning and stimulus-response relations using taught binned-data procedures.
Infer circuit function from recordings, lesions and stimulation while distinguishing correlation from causation.
Explain synaptic plasticity and representative circuit disorders using mechanistic evidence.

practice: Analyze public neural recordings with spreadsheet or supplied analysis tools and defend causal circuit interpretations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain organism-environment interactions across scales.
decks.title: Ecology

outcomes.description: Estimate population abundance and vital rates and project discrete growth with explicit sampling assumptions.
Evaluate competition, predation and community-assembly hypotheses using field evidence.
Construct ecosystem energy and nutrient budgets and predict disturbance responses.

practice: Design quadrat or mark-recapture sampling and analyze population, community and ecosystem datasets.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer evolutionary processes from comparative and population evidence.
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology

outcomes.description: Distinguish evolutionary mechanisms and calculate elementary allele-frequency changes.
Construct small parsimony and distance trees and assess character conflict and support.
Evaluate speciation and macroevolutionary hypotheses using reproductive, fossil and comparative evidence.

practice: Compare evolutionary explanations and construct phylogenies from small explicit character datasets.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Test proximate and evolutionary explanations of behavior.
decks.title: Behavioral Biology

outcomes.description: Construct ethograms and design observations controlling observer bias and pseudoreplication.
Analyze foraging, mating and simple evolutionary-game payoffs under explicit assumptions.
Discriminate kinship, reciprocity, communication and learning hypotheses with comparative experiments.

practice: Code behavior from approved videos and evaluate competing adaptive and learning explanations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Turn sequence measurements into defensible biological inference.
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics

outcomes.description: Implement dynamic-programming alignment and evaluate sequence annotation evidence.
Process read and variant representations and assess mapping, coverage and population-reference biases.
Analyze normalized expression counts with supplied statistical software and control batch effects and multiplicity.

practice: Build a versioned small-genome analysis pipeline with explicit file formats, quality controls and privacy assessment.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Quantify genetic change and infer population history.
decks.title: Population Genetics

outcomes.description: Derive deterministic selection recursions and finite-population drift probabilities.
Calculate linkage disequilibrium and elementary coalescent waiting-time predictions.
Estimate diversity and differentiation and distinguish demographic from selective explanations.

practice: Derive population models and analyze allele-frequency and genealogy summaries with uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Integrate molecular mechanisms into testable quantitative models.
decks.title: Systems Biology

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric and rate-equation networks and analyze conservation and feedback stability.
Estimate kinetic parameters by locally taught nonlinear least squares and test sensitivity and identifiability.
Derive chemical master-equation transitions and implement Gillespie simulation with distributional checks.

practice: Implement deterministic and stochastic gene circuits and design perturbations that resolve parameter ambiguity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Explain pathological failures of biological regulation.
decks.title: Disease Biology and Pathology

outcomes.description: Explain host-pathogen damage and distinguish direct virulence from immune-mediated injury.
Analyze oncogenic alterations, clonal selection and resistance mechanisms from molecular evidence.
Compare degeneration, regeneration and fibrosis mechanisms across tissues.

practice: Interpret anonymized pathology and molecular datasets and distinguish mechanistic evidence from clinical recommendations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer population-health patterns and intervention effects.
decks.title: Epidemiology

outcomes.description: Calculate epidemiological rates, standardized comparisons and screening predictive values.
Construct causal diagrams and appraise confounding, selection and measurement bias in study designs.
Use locally taught discrete transmission models to compare interventions and equity-sensitive tradeoffs.

practice: Analyze an outbreak line list and critically compare intervention evidence without assuming randomized identification.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Translate ecological evidence into accountable management choices.
decks.title: Conservation Biology

outcomes.description: Design biodiversity monitoring and adjust simple abundance estimates for imperfect detection.
Project viability using locally taught age-structured tables and evaluate restoration and connectivity options.
Compare management options using uncertainty, costs, Indigenous knowledge governance and stakeholder values.

practice: Prepare a conservation decision brief using monitoring data, spreadsheet viability projections and explicit value tradeoffs.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Develop graduate methods for ecological and evolutionary inference.
decks.title: Advanced Ecology and Evolution

outcomes.description: Construct spatial patch and dispersal models and analyze persistence and connectivity.
Derive coupled ecological and evolutionary dynamics and assess invasion and stability.
Fit hierarchical occupancy and demographic models and assess observation-process identifiability.

practice: Implement spatial and hierarchical ecological models and compare mechanistic and observational sources of uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Infer molecular structure and function through physical measurements.
decks.title: Structural Biology and Molecular Biophysics

outcomes.description: Explain diffraction, cryo-EM reconstruction and NMR restraints and assess resolution and model validation.
Calculate binding and folding thermodynamics and infer conformational populations from measurements.
Design mutational and biophysical tests that discriminate structure-function hypotheses.

practice: Use documented reconstruction and refinement software on supplied data; analyze map-model agreement and propose independent functional tests.

decks.subject: biology
decks.description: Test mechanistic explanations of dynamic cellular organization.
decks.title: Advanced Cell Biology

outcomes.description: Derive compartment and reaction-diffusion models for trafficking, gradients and cellular self-organization.
Analyze cell and tissue force measurements using bounded elastic and active-stress models.
Design quantitative live-cell perturbations that distinguish transport, mechanical and regulatory mechanisms.

practice: Analyze supplied live-cell trajectories and force maps, derive competing models and specify discriminating experiments.
